title: Partial observation, causal filtering, and identifiability
task: Use the fixed local-level state-space model r_t=mu_t+eps_t, mu_(t+1)=phi*mu_t+eta_(t+1), independent Gaussian eps variance R and eta variance Q, in bps units. Derive the causal Kalman prior, observation predictive variance, gain, posterior, and next prior. Implement kalman_filter(returns, phi, q, r, m0=0.0, p0=None) returning a dict of same-length numeric lists pred_mean, pred_var, post_mean, post_var. pred_mean[i] is the prediction of returns[i] BEFORE observing it; pred_var includes observation noise. Initial latent prior is m0 and p0, default q/(1-phi**2); after observing each value transition with phi and q. Assume abs(phi)<1, q>0, r>0. For the real-data diagnostic freeze phi=.95, Q=.04 bps^2, and R=sample variance (ddof=1) of nonmissing TRAIN r_bps. These are illustrative assumptions, not fitted market truth. Run each contiguous segment in frame separately, reset to stationary prior only at a real gap, carry the filter across the train/validation boundary within the same segment, and report validation n, one-step MSE, zero-mean baseline MSE, Gaussian 95% predictive coverage, and the last five validation forecasts. Check prediction alignment with code. Derive stationary observation autocovariances and discuss when phi,Q,R are identifiable from their theoretical values, including phi=0. Explain why several days of returns and apparent predictive interval coverage do not establish a true hidden drift or stable future edge. Produce final JSON keys derivation, python (self-contained implementation), empirical (actual executed statistics), limitations, conclusion. Use python tools to calculate and check your answer; do not invent numerical results.

title: Finite-horizon stochastic control with costs and forced liquidation
task: Define a transparent toy stochastic-control problem. At each decision observe a state z in {0,1} and previous position p in {-1,0,1}; choose q in {-1,0,1}. One-period gross return conditional on z has mean mus[z] and variance variances[z], in bps units. Charge c*abs(q-p) NOW and subtract lam*q*q*variances[z]/2 as a one-period additive risk penalty. Next z follows transition[z,:]. After the last return liquidate, charging c*abs(q). Derive the Bellman recursion and base case, and clarify that additive stage variance penalties are not generally variance of terminal cumulative PnL. Implement solve_dp(horizon,c,mus,variances,lam,transition) -> {'values': nested numeric lists, 'actions': nested numeric lists}, arrays of shape (horizon+1,3,2), p order [-1,0,1], z order [0,1]. values[0,p,z]=-c*abs(p), actions[0,p,z]=0. With n steps remaining evaluate q*mus[z]-lam*q*q*variances[z]/2-c*abs(q-p)+sum(transition[z,z2]*values[n-1,q,z2]). Among objective ties within 1e-10 choose smallest abs(q-p), then smallest abs(q), then smallest q. Demonstrate a case where preserving an existing position is preferable to opening that same position from flat, or explicitly state if the chosen parameters do not exhibit it. For real data define state z_t=1 if current completed one-minute return x_bps>=0 else 0. Estimate mus[z]=mean of NEXT y_bps conditional on current z, variances[z]=sample variance of those y_bps (ddof=1), transition[z,z2] from consecutive signs of x_bps and y_bps, using ONLY pairs_train. Fix horizon=15, lam=.04, c=manifest fixed_cost_proxies_bps.one_way_fee_only. This is a first-order, finite-state approximation to test, not an asserted true Markov market. Compute values and actions for all previous positions and states at 15 steps. On validation, report conditional mean prediction MSE and zero prediction baseline MSE; do not refit. Check base case, terminal liquidation, and at least one value/action by independent enumeration. Discuss omitted history, state uncertainty, funding, and missing training spread/funding data and fee-only execution costs. Final JSON keys derivation, python (self-contained implementation), empirical (actual executed estimates, transition, horizon-15 values/actions and validation metrics), limitations, conclusion. Use python tools; no invented results or profitable-rule search.

title: Robust decision under conditional-mean estimation error
task: From flat, hold a position a in [-1,1] for ONE minute and close it; net return aY-k*abs(a). Model conditional mean as beta0+beta1*x, but suppose at this x the true mean lies in [mhat-u,mhat+u], and conditional variance is fixed v>0. Derive max_a min_mu {a*mu-k*abs(a)-lam*a*a*v/2}. Implement robust_position(mhat,u,k,lam,v) -> float for finite mhat, u>=0,k>=0,lam>=0,v>0, including lam=0 and threshold ties (choose zero at a no-trade tie). Explain exactly what is and is not guaranteed if the true model falls outside the interval. Fit ONE prespecified OLS regression y_bps=beta0+beta1*x_bps+error using only pairs_train. Under explicitly stated iid Gaussian homoskedastic/exogenous regression assumptions, use residual variance SSE/(n-2) and the two-sided 95% POINTWISE Student-t conditional-MEAN interval half-width u(x)=t_(.975,n-2)*s*sqrt(1/n+(x-xbar)^2/Sxx). Distinguish it from a new-observation prediction interval, whose variance includes an additional 1. Freeze lam=.04, k=manifest fixed_cost_proxies_bps.round_trip_fee_only. Report train n,beta0,beta1,residual variance, t critical, residual lag-1 correlation (only adjacent pairs in the same contiguous segment), validation n,prediction MSE,zero baseline MSE, robust trade count, and mean proxy net bps per validation opportunity (zero on abstentions) using a*y-k*abs(a). Report separately the number of nominal Gaussian prediction intervals covering validation y and explain why this cannot measure coverage of the unobserved conditional mean. Check position formula numerically against direct maximization. Do not change feature/horizon/confidence level to find profit. Critique dependence, nonstationarity, pointwise versus selection/uniform guarantees, and missing training spread/funding data and fee-only execution costs. Final JSON keys derivation, python (self-contained implementation), empirical (actual executed statistics and frozen regression parameters), limitations, conclusion. Use python tools and actual printed statistics, not guessed numbers.
